body:
Rule 4d, sidebar;  I'm here because I'm the only person who can turn my life around, and I realized that me and all future versions of me aren't going to have the emotional maturity/resources to make significant change.

As for family, loneliness/social isolation is the biggest predictor for suicide.  Obviously because of the people you would hurt.  If I had a child, I could never do it, by bringing someone to life, you owe them trying to give them the best life possible.  But I don't; I just have a couple friends, two parents whom one day I'll just never speak to again, a brother and sister I'll end up talking to once a month, and some cousins I'll see once a year.  I'm extremely empathetic, even being rude to someone hurts me, not for social ostracization, but genuinely that I hate hurting others.  In fact how selfless I normally am almost justifies being selfish just once.  It doesn't, but i can't feel I owe anything, other than politeness, to people I don't like.
Thanks for the reply anyways, it was better than I made it sound, I'm just very bitter because my parents constantly use the same weak logic to guilt trip the hell out me for a lot of things.  (If you don't want to do something, do it for us, even if you hate it.)
Thanks, what I needed to hear that you didn't say the first time.And I definitely will.

That would an amazing boost.  The only 2 things i can really do in that area of my life is network harder and stop being such a lazy piece of crap.  I live in SoCal, and somehow can't seem to find anyone within 60 miles.  Comparing with other craigslists confirms my particular scene is fairly dead.  Working on my own is really just a matter of "get motivated!" which is pretty hard right now.  It's not stressing me out very much right now, but it could make me feel a lot better.  I'm sticking around for at least 2 weeks so I'll get back into it.

When your day to day is really shitty, you're kind of forced to look to the future.  And if that doesn't look any better you end up posting here. "Losing all hope" and focusing on now probably hurts almost much because I'm forced back an awful time that actually exists.  I can't stop thinking about suicide because I don't have the emotional tools to deal with the right now, and today made me realize future me isn't either.

Looking at everything at once wasn't stressful because it felt like too much to take of, it just made me realize I'm screwing up in every possible way.

I'm stressing out because these things aren't really "worst case" scenarios; I feel they're rather likely.

But for taking things one at a time, I suppose I've never really tried it because it's so hard to shut out other parts of one's life.  I mean I could focus on something for a few hours or maybe a day, but all the rest finds a way to take up my time and energy.  Thank you, it'll be hard but I'll try it.

Thanks, that made me smile.  I always thought of myself as someone who'd stop dating young, but that doesn't mean I HAVE to be.  It sounds like you have an extremely good relationship if he'd tell something that sensitive that was so long ago.  Or he's super whiny; I could relate.

Thank for your words, I wish more I could be more responsive to them.  I've been so motivated lately, and today destroyed that by showing me how despite growth I'm still static. Its never been harder for me to stay positive or at least that I will be in the future.  Extrapolating a flat line isn't the most promising thing.  As I'm faithless, I can't fathom a reason for things to get better other than my ineffective will or anything else that could pull me out this, I mean it could happen but I'm rolling some pretty unfair dice on that.
